tour.locked: Sign in to open this one — it reads your own data.
tour.launch_caption: Walks through every feature and where it lives, and tells you what changed in the latest release.
tour.finished: Tour finished — reopen it any time from Profile.
tour.news_intro: Shipped since you were last here.
tour.welcome_body: TopStocks turns a broker statement into your real numbers: FIFO lots, P/L in your own currency at the ECB rate of each trade's own date, and what your tax office will want. This tour walks through each feature, says whether your account has it switched on, and takes you to it. Two minutes, and you can leave and come back at any point.
tour.import_body: Drop a statement: every row is parsed and previewed before anything is written to your ledger. Revolut (CSV and PDF), Revolut crypto, Trading 212, DEGIRO, Interactive Brokers, ClickTrade / Saxo and a generic CSV are recognised, and re-importing the same statement never duplicates a row. No statement to hand yet? **Load an example statement** puts a real one through the same parse, preview and commit, and **Clear last import** takes it back out again. Not ready to hand over a real statement? **Use demo transactions** on the Portfolio page fills the ledger with a made-up book of seven well-known stocks so every tab has something in it; it is labelled as demo wherever it shows, and your first real import deletes it. Everything else in the app — positions, P/L, allocation, tax, dividends, fees — derives from this one ledger.
tour.positions_body: Your open lots with live prices, market value and weight in your reporting currency, plus which broker each holding actually sits in — a ticker split across two custodians shows as a split. Every ticker cell links through to its full page.
tour.risk_body: Two different questions, two sections. **Real return** is what your book actually did: time-weighted return (flow-adjusted, so a deposit never reads as a gain), money-weighted return (IRR), volatility and worst drawdown. **Risk of the current basket** is about what you hold today — allocation by sector, geography, currency and broker.
tour.tax_body: Sales matched against your lots — FIFO, LIFO, average cost or UK S104, whichever your country uses — realized gains per year net of commissions, and your jurisdiction's own rules on top. Twelve are implemented (ES, US, UK, DE, FR, IT, IE, PT, CA, AU, AE, CH), each with its own brackets, allowances, reporting flags and reporting currency. Set your tax residence in Profile: it decides which rules run and which currency the ledger is replayed in.
tour.income_body: Dividends per year and per position, with withholding and the credit you can claim — and, beside them, what your shares were **entitled** to: every company's dividend history priced by the shares your ledger held the day before each ex-date, so a payment your statement never carried still shows up, and next year's income is estimated on today's holdings. The **Fees** tab then separates what the broker charged from what the spread cost you: each execution is measured against the midpoint of its own session, so the markup that never appears on a statement becomes a number.
tour.pulse_body: Where the market is heading, read against your own book — ranked by how much of it you actually need. The top card answers it in five seconds: **risk appetite** as a 0-100 score on its own meter, with a ghost pin where the score stood a month ago, and beside it the same regime restated as what it does to your basket. **Why** opens the number up: all eight inputs — trend, breadth, volatility, term structure, credit, stocks-versus-bonds, junk demand and emerging markets — each with its own bar, a tick at where it stood a month ago and its raw level, so the score is auditable rather than a black box; an input that could not be built is named and greyed rather than quietly dropped. Alongside it, four readings that only exist as trends: how many indices and sectors are above their own trend, the stock/bond correlation (positive means both legs fall together), and which of the four rates regimes the last quarter describes. **Your book against this regime** measures your basket's sensitivity to equities, rates, credit and the dollar — each pill is the three-month drift, which is the regime moving under you without your having traded. **The detail** keeps the six long tables — indices, gauges, rates, inflation, rotation and cross-asset — behind one tab strip, every row the same shape: the level, the change over 1w / 1m / 3m / 12m, a sparkline, and whether the series is in an uptrend or turning. Every row there carries an **i** beside its name that says what the series is and how to read it, because “MOVE” and “2s10s” are not names that explain themselves.
tour.market_body: Price and chart with a zoom range that reports the move over exactly the window you selected, plus financials, estimates, insider activity and news. Every KPI carries where it came from: **Fact** is verifiable in a filing, **Consensus** is analyst estimates, **Derived** is computed here. The search box at the top of the page works from anywhere in the app. **Analyze with AI** in the header hands the whole company to the assistant — one click asks it about the business, the fundamentals, the valuation against its own history and how the position fits your book (funds and coins get their own question).
tour.screener_body: Filter the market on the metrics you care about, and see which of your holdings and watchlist names report next — with the result itself, surprise and reaction, once it lands.
tour.assistant_body: The chat panel on the right, reachable from every page, with your real book in hand: it reads your positions, live quotes, filings and the web, keeps long-term memory across conversations, and picks the analysis skill that fits the question. An empty thread opens with a few suggestions built from your own watchlist, so it has something useful to say before you have imported anything. It runs keyless on the shared TopStocks chain within a daily cap; connect your own provider key for no cap and your choice of model. You can ask out loud as well: the microphone on the composer records a note, transcribes it and sends the transcript as the question — the audio itself is never stored. While an answer is being written the send button becomes a stop button: press it and the answer stops where it is, keeping whatever it had already written. A connection that drops mid-answer is not read as a stop: the question is answered again the next time you open the app.
tour.notify_body: A portfolio digest in the evening and price alerts during market hours, on Telegram. The digest ranks the day by what each holding did to your book in your reporting currency rather than by the loudest percentage, sets it against the S&P 500, and lists the week's ex-dividend dates and the payments already received. Link your account once from the Notifications tab and the toggles start working; the jobs run server-side, so nothing depends on you having the app open.
tour.investor_body: Risk tolerance, horizon, focus and constraints. The assistant reads it before answering, so the analysis is framed for your mandate instead of a generic one. The **focus** areas do one more thing: the watchlist tab then offers example tickers from them that you do not already follow — examples to look at, never recommendations, and adding them removes nothing you have.
tour.prefs_body: Reporting currency, language, tax residence and the bracket inputs your jurisdiction reads, grouped into three cards; the tax card states what the choice decides (cost currency, share matching, tax year) instead of describing it. Nothing here has a Save button — every change is written as you make it. It is also where the ledger exports to CSV, where an account deletes itself, and where this tour lives whenever you want it again.
tour.daily_body: One AI card at the top of Home, generated once a day (it turns over at 09:00 in your own timezone): a headline and three or four lines on what to look at today — the day's move, the name that drove it, a print due this week, a position sitting at a 52-week edge. It reads the numbers the page already computed, and if no model answers it falls back to the same facts without the prose.
tour.news_2026_09_tax_body: ES, US, UK, DE, FR, IT, IE, PT, CA and AU, each with its own lot matching, brackets and reporting flags — pick your residence in Profile. Positions also record which broker holds them now.
tour.news_2026_09_daily_body: One AI briefing a day on the dashboard, on the numbers Home already has — no prompt to write.
tour.news_2026_09_chat_body: It now decides what to gather before it answers, and remembers across conversations.
tour.news_2026_09_askai_body: Any ticker's header now carries an Analyze with AI button: it opens the assistant with a full question about that company — business, fundamentals, valuation against its own history, risks and fit with your book — already asked.
tour.news_2026_09_fees_body: Commissions and estimated spread per broker — the execution cost your statement never itemises.
tour.news_2026_09_demo_body: The Portfolio page can now fill itself with a made-up book of seven well-known stocks, so you can see positions, risk, dividends, fees and the tax report working before importing anything — your first real import removes it.
tour.news_2026_09_guest_body: The Portfolio page now opens for guests on the demo book — positions, allocation and risk, dividends, fees and the tax report, all filled in and nothing to sign in for. Signing in swaps that book for the one you import.
tour.news_2026_09_pulse_body: A new page built around direction rather than level, and ranked for a five-second read: a 0-100 risk-appetite score with its eight inputs laid open beside it, your own basket's sensitivities and how far they have drifted, and six tables — indices, gauges, rates, inflation, rotation and cross-asset — behind one tab strip, every row carrying its 1w/1m/3m/12m change, a sparkline and a trend label.
tour.news_2026_09_profile_body: Every setting is a row with its own explanation, grouped into Interface, Tax residence and Data — the tax card now states the rules your jurisdiction actually applies, and the whole ledger exports as CSV.
tour.news_2026_09_digest_body: The evening digest now ranks the day by each holding's contribution in your own currency, so a 7% pop on a small position stops outranking a 2% drift on a large one. It sets your day against the **S&P 500**, names the **currency** share of the move when the exchange rate did real work, and shrinks to a single line when the session was flat and the calendar empty.
tour.news_2026_09_digestcal_title: Dividends and results in the digest
tour.news_2026_09_digestcal_body: Two new blocks. **Dividends** lists the ex-dates falling in the next week with the cash they should pay on what you hold, plus what already landed; **Just reported** covers the quarters that printed in the last few days — beat or miss, EPS against the estimate, and the move across the print. A Monday digest also says so when your last statement import has gone stale.
tour.news_2026_09_digestlinks_body: Every ticker in a digest or an alert is now a link straight to its page, and the message carries buttons for wherever it points — **Portfolio**, **Earnings** when something reported, **Import statement** when your book has gone stale. Alerts also say what you actually hold in the name that fired: the share count and where it sits against your cost.
tour.news_2026_09_weekly_body: A new message, once a week, for the question five daily digests never answer: how is this going. Week, month and **year-to-date** in money and percent with the index beside each, the names that actually moved the book, the cash that landed, the week ahead — and how **concentrated** you have become, with the drift since last Sunday. Switch it off in Profile → Notifications.
tour.watchlist_body: The list every other page reads: Overview, Screener, Earnings and the ticker picker all run on it. Add a name by **searching** it — your own list, coins, funds, the SEC company map and every venue Yahoo quotes, so a symbol arrives with its real name instead of being spelled from memory. **Groups** are the app's grouping primitive: a ticker can sit in several, the list can be grouped by them, and Overview renders a section per group. Everything you edit here writes immediately.
tour.news_2026_09_watchlist_body: Adding a ticker is a **search** across your list, coins, funds, the SEC map and worldwide listings — no more typing a symbol into a blank grid row. **Groups** are a picker rather than a comma string, the list can be **grouped by** them, and a group can be renamed or dissolved from its own header. Every edit saves as you make it, and phones get one control row per holding instead of a grid that pans sideways.
tour.news_2026_09_1_tips_title: Every row on Pulse now explains itself
tour.news_2026_09_1_tips_body: The detail tables name things without defining them — VIX, MOVE, SKEW, 2s10s, RSP over SPY. Each row now carries a small **i** beside its name: hover it, or tap it on a phone, and it says in one sentence what the series is and how to read it. Sixty-two of them, across indices, volatility, rates, inflation, rotation, factors and cross-asset.
tour.news_2026_09_1_voice_body: The composer now carries a **microphone**, beside the paperclip: record the question and it arrives as text, transcribed on the same keyless chain the answers come from. Only the transcript is kept — the recording is dropped as soon as it has been read — and the turn is badged as spoken, so a misheard ticker explains itself on reload. It is worth most on a phone, where typing out a five-line question is the worst part of asking it.
tour.news_2026_09_1_stop_title: Stop an answer while it is being written
tour.news_2026_09_1_stop_body: The send button becomes a **stop** button while the assistant is working: press it and the answer stops where it is. A turn runs through routing, searches and a stream, which is long enough to see it heading the wrong way. What had already been written stays on the thread, badged as stopped rather than left reading like the model trailed off, and the field opens again for the next question.
tour.news_2026_09_1_splits_body: Most statements print trades and no corporate actions, so a share count bought before a **20:1** and sold after it never adds up — and that sell used to be rejected with nothing you could do about it. The preview now checks the split history of the ticker that came up short and files the split as a row of its own, so the ledger gets it too. The preview also reads in your language: the reason a row was flagged, the column headings and the buy/sell verbs.
tour.news_2026_09_1_divest_title: Dividends you were owed, not just the ones imported
tour.news_2026_09_1_divest_body: The **Dividends** tab now opens with three figures — since you started, this year, and what the next 12 months pay if you sell nothing — and estimates income from your own shares: every company's dividend history times the shares you held the day before each ex-date. A **Not recorded** column shows what never reached your ledger. Estimates are gross and never touch the tax figures.
tour.news_2026_09_1_tickerlinks_body: Symbols now carry their logo and link straight to the company's page wherever they appear — the dividend payers table, an import preview in the chat, the watchlist suggestions on **Profile**.
tour.news_2026_09_1_ibkr_title: IBKR statements in Spanish, and ones with no trades
tour.news_2026_09_1_ibkr_body: Interactive Brokers writes the activity statement in the account's own language, and the importer now reads the **Spanish** section and column names as well as the English ones. A statement covering a quiet period has no trades in it at all — there the **open positions** block imports instead, one buy per holding at the broker's own average cost. The cost basis is exact; the dates are not, since every lot lands on the statement day, so import a statement with real trades over it before trusting the tax report's holding periods.
tour.news_2026_09_1_amount_title: Two more statement shapes import cleanly
tour.news_2026_09_1_amount_body: Some exports print only the row's **total** — the cash that actually moved — and leave the per-share price at zero. That is how a dividend is quoted everywhere, and how a few brokers quote trades too. The importer now maps that column as well and works the unit price back out of it. Others write the action as a sentence that differs in every row ("YOU BOUGHT PROSHARES ULTRAPRO QQQ (TQQQ)"), where an exact match found nothing and the whole file imported as zero rows; the verb is now read out of the sentence.
tour.news_2026_09_1_tgtext_title: The Telegram bot says when it cannot read you
tour.news_2026_09_1_tgtext_body: Send the bot a **voice note**, a photo or a file and it used to do nothing at all: no text, so no answer, and nothing to say why. It now replies that it only reads text — true whoever sent it, so it is said before the account-linking check rather than after. A pin or an edited message still passes in silence, because nobody is waiting on those.
tour.news_2026_09_1_hover_title: Chart tooltips read like the rest of the app
tour.news_2026_09_1_hover_body: Hovering a candlestick printed Plotly's own four-line dump, with the close buried among three equals. A hover is now one metric row: muted label, bold close, and the bar's **change on the previous close** beside it in the gain/loss pair, with open, high and low a step down. The rounded corners and shadow now reach the shared-axis tooltips on the price, portfolio and fundamentals charts, which had been drawing square.
tour.news_2026_09_1_isin_title: Holdings that came in as an ISIN now read as themselves
tour.news_2026_09_1_isin_body: DEGIRO's export prints no symbol and Saxo's prints one for a venue Yahoo does not use, so those trades import under the **ISIN** — and every table read "US81762P1021" where it meant ServiceNow. The app now looks the ISIN up itself, once, so the import preview, the positions and the logos all show the symbol and the company name. The ledger still stores exactly what the broker wrote, which is what your `aliases:` mapping overrides when you want a different listing.
tour.news_2026_09_2_splitfix_body: A share bought before a **20:1** split and never sold used to keep the share count and the price the trade ticket carried, so the position read as a deep loss against a post-split market price. **Check for missing splits** on the Import page now compares each holding's buy price against the market close of that day: when the price is still on the old scale it names the split, shows what the share count becomes, and adds the row on your say-so. The money you paid never changes — only the shares behind it, and the average buy price that follows. The price chart follows: your buy and sell markers now sit on the candles' own scale, so an old lot plots where it really was and its return to today is the real one.
tour.news_2026_09_2_peersearch_body: The comps table's extra peers used to be a comma-separated box: you had to know the symbol by heart, and a typo just produced an empty column. It is now the **same live search as the top bar** — type a name or a symbol and the watchlist, the fund catalog, the SEC company map and a worldwide Yahoo lookup answer as you type, so a European competitor you never followed goes into the table by name. Each pick becomes a chip you can drop again.
tour.news_2026_09_2_transfers_title: Shares that changed broker, not owner
tour.news_2026_09_2_transfers_body: Move a holding to another broker and the statements disagree about what happened: the old broker prints the departure as a **sale at the day's market price**, the new one just lists the shares as a balance. Your book then reported a capital gain nobody made, restarted the holding period, and taxed the whole thing. Transfers are now their own kind of ledger row — no gain is realized, the original purchase date and cost basis carry across, and only the broker holding the shares changes. DEGIRO exports are read directly (a departure carries no order id, no venue and no commission, because nobody traded), and for a book already imported the wrong way the Import page offers to repair it: it pairs a sale with the arrival that carries the **same cost basis**, which is the one thing a real sale-and-repurchase could not produce.
tour.news_2026_09_2_fbvoice_body: **Send feedback** now writes in the same composer the assistant uses, with the **microphone inside the box** next to the send arrow. Record instead of typing and the note is transcribed and sent in one go — the same deal a voice note in the chat makes, so say the ticker clearly.
tour.news_2026_09_2_fbshot_title: Send the screen with the report
tour.news_2026_09_2_fbshot_body: **Send feedback** can now carry a picture of the screen behind it — tick the box and the browser captures the page as it is right then, the modal itself left out. It is off by default and shown to you before it goes, because that picture carries your own figures.
tour.news_2026_09_2_mobilechat_body: The assistant's controls above the box are down to one on a phone, which gives the reading back the room they were taking. **Internet is simply always on** there rather than a chip you could leave switched off by accident — at a desk it is still a toggle, and still yours.
tour.news_2026_09_2_uae_title: The United Arab Emirates, and its zero
tour.news_2026_09_2_uae_body: Pick **United Arab Emirates** as your tax residence and the tab replays your book in **dirhams** and reports what it honestly owes: nothing. There is no personal income tax and no capital gains tax there, at any amount and any holding period — so a losing year carries nothing forward either, and the tab says so instead of promising you a deduction. The one boundary worth knowing is named on the page: run the same portfolio through a licensed entity and 9% corporate tax above AED 375,000 applies to *that* entity.
tour.news_2026_09_2_swiss_title: Switzerland, where the gain is exempt
tour.news_2026_09_2_swiss_body: **Switzerland** joins the tax residences: private capital gains are outside taxable income under art. 16 para. 3 DBG, so the tab replays your book in **francs** and owes nothing on it. It never shows that zero on its own — the **KS 36** safe harbour comes with it (six months' holding, turnover under 5× the portfolio, gains under half your income, no leverage, no speculative derivatives), because failing one of those five turns every gain into ordinary income plus AHV.
tour.news_2026_09_2_taxfallback_title: The tax tab admits when it doesn't know your country
tour.news_2026_09_2_taxfallback_body: Until now a filer in a country we don't model read **Spanish brackets over their own book** with nothing on the page saying so. The tab now says it outright: your gains and losses are real, the rules on top of them are borrowed, and here is where to fix it. Twelve countries are modelled — if yours is one, pick it in Profile.
tour.news_2026_09_2_kpimatch_title: Totals that measure the same shares
tour.news_2026_09_2_kpimatch_body: When a price does not arrive — a throttled feed, a symbol the provider drops — the position still carries its cost, and the tiles divided the whole book's **cost basis** by the part of it that got priced: an intact portfolio reading -60%. Cost basis and market value now cover the same rows, a line under them says how many positions were left out, and a **weight** no longer grows to fill a missing name's place.
tour.news_2026_09_2_onebook_body: DEGIRO's export names a security by its **ISIN** and IBKR by its **symbol**, so shares moved between the two sat in the book twice: the departure left a lot open under one name while the arrival opened another, the cost basis counted twice and the weights computed over a portfolio you never had. The replay now reads both labels as one security and keeps the tradeable symbol.
tour.news_2026_09_2_wht_title: Withholding that lands on its dividend
tour.news_2026_09_2_wht_body: An IBKR statement prints the tax withheld at source on a line of its own, and it had to be copied onto the dividend by hand — until it was, the year reported its **gross as its net**. A tax line that can only mean one payment (same ticker, day and currency) is now applied to it on import; a restatement, or two payments on one day, is still left to you, because guessing there is how a year's withholding doubles.
tour.news_2026_09_2_pricedmoves_title: Prices for holdings that were moved, not bought
tour.news_2026_09_2_pricedmoves_body: The price download read your **buy and sell rows** to decide what to fetch, so a holding that arrived on a transfer — shares moved between brokers, or an opening balance off a statement — was never asked for a price and read **n/a** all the way down the table. It is now driven by what the book holds, under the same name the replay gives it, so a book assembled from two brokers prices in full.
tour.news_2026_09_2_venue_title: The listing your statement is actually reporting
tour.news_2026_09_2_venue_body: Interactive Brokers prints a bare local symbol on every market it lists, and a bare `ASML` is the **Nasdaq ADR in dollars**, not the Amsterdam share in euros the statement is reporting. Imports now read the listing venue from the statement's instrument table and book the holding against it (`ASML.AS`), so a European line is not priced off its US twin. A venue we don't recognise is left exactly as your broker wrote it.
tour.news_2026_09_2_chatmoves_title: Broker moves caught in the assistant too
tour.news_2026_09_2_chatmoves_body: Import a statement in the chat and it now asks the same question the Import page does: **do these shares look like they only changed broker?** Your old broker prints the departure as a sale, so the book reports a gain nobody made — and a file imported here never went past the page that offered to fix it. The repair is the same one, on the same button.
tour.news_2026_09_2_resume_title: Answers that survive leaving the app
tour.news_2026_09_2_resume_body: Lock the phone or switch apps while the assistant is writing and the connection goes with the page: the reply used to stop mid-word and stay that way, half a sentence filed as the final word. It now tells **a Stop you pressed from a connection that dropped** — the question whose answer the connection cut is answered again the moment you come back, and one you stopped yourself stays exactly where you cut it.
